views.label: $\Lambda > 0$

start.text: the circles grow faster than the distance out to them, and nothing in Euclidean space carries the slice on toward the singular axis

end.text: the tube runs on to the far axis $\rho = \pi\ell$, where the circles of $\psi$ close

stops: Inside $\rho = 0.29\,\ell$ the circles grow faster than the distance out to them, $g_{\rho\rho} < (\partial_\rho\sqrt{g_{\phi\phi}})^2$, and no surface of revolution in Euclidean space carries the slice on to the axis.

views.label: $\Lambda < 0$

start.text: the axis $\rho = 0$, regular, where the circles of $\phi$ shrink to a point

end.text: the sheet runs on toward the light cone, to $\rho \to \infty$

stops: At every $\rho > 0$ the circles grow faster than the distance out to them, $g_{\rho\rho} < (\partial_\rho\sqrt{g_{\phi\phi}})^2$, and no surface of revolution in Euclidean space carries the surface; Minkowski space carries it.
caption: Bonnor's universe ($\sigma = 0$) at one moment ($z = 0$), drawn in Minkowski space about its regular axis.
